title: Wildfire of "exceptional scale" burning near Paris
facts: Two firefighting aircraft were deployed south of Paris to combat a massive wildfire.
A large wildfire ignited late Sunday afternoon in the Fontainebleau forest located approximately 40 miles southeast of Paris.
The wildfire burned through roughly 1,900 acres of land by early Monday morning.
The spread of the wildfire prompted authorities to partially close a major highway south of Paris.
Firefighting aircraft were forced to halt aerial operations upon the arrival of nightfall.
Emergency personnel evacuated around 15 homes in the village of Vaudoue due to the spreading blaze.
Approximately 400 firefighters were deployed to contain the Fontainebleau forest fire.
The wildfire occurred immediately prior to France's July 14 national holiday weekend.
The wildfire disrupted high-speed railway services connecting Paris to southeastern France.
The Paris region experienced its third distinct heatwave since May 2026.
Recent heatwaves caused multiple temperature records to be broken across several European countries.
Health authorities in France, Belgium, Britain, and Spain estimated thousands of excess deaths due to the 2026 heatwaves.
The World Weather Attribution group concluded that the June 2026 heatwaves would have been virtually impossible without climate change.
The Seine-et-Marne fire service coordinated efforts to defend multiple towns threatened by the blaze.
Regional highway traffic was heavily disrupted during the opening departure weekend of the French summer holiday season.
